added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arms at the same command: baseline_suite at f845e102ac lists three failing ids (test_a_held_open_tick_keeps_the_lease_fresh_and_refuses_a_second_station, test_the_lease_is_renewed_while_the_heartbeat_write_is_blocked, test_a_replaced_lease_refuses_every_write_and_stops_the_loop) in gate-base.log, and after_suite at 1898660cc4 lists none in gate-head.log, so the change adds zero ids. Those three are the new test's own cases, absent from the base tree's file, so the base arm's red is a shape failure (run_station refuses the injected keyword arguments) rather than the defect reproducing, and the negative control in gate-negative-control.log carries the falsification instead: 3 failed, EXIT=1, the held-open case among them.

0.reason: follow-up: lift one lease renewer with an on-loss callback into host_lease and use it for both promotion and the station

1.reason: follow-up: guard connect()'s schema and identity writes too, for a handle opened after the loss

2.reason: follow-up: assert each store write method refuses, not that some write refused

findings.text: _PromotionLeaseRenewer already renews a HostLease from a daemon thread at LEASE_RENEW_SECONDS with start and stop, and LeaseBeat duplicates that loop; one renewer lifted into reckon/crew/host_lease.py with an on-loss callback would serve both, but the node was fenced out of every file that could hold it.

connect() creates the schema and calls _ensure_station_identity() without guard.check(), so a store handle whose connection is opened after the loss still writes identity rows; that is narrower than the done-when's 'no store write of any kind', though it needs a handle opened after mark_lost, which the station's own two handles are not.

the arm asserts only that some write was refused, not that each write method refuses, so a regression removing guard.check() from sweep_retention, write_cursor or delete_obligation leaves this case green while the twelfth of the done-when's writes it was protecting is unguarded again.

the module docstring narrates the previous behaviour ('The lease used to be renewed between ticks') instead of stating the mechanism, which the repository's naming rule bans in source comments and docstrings.

the '# module' header line names the head worktree's station.py while the arm actually imported the scratch base tree; I confirmed by importing it directly that .../base-tree-AjDy/reckon/crew/station.py is the module resolved and that it has no LeaseBeat, so the log's provenance line is wrong even though the manifest's measurement_module records the base tree correctly.
